what: State Street is a custody bank. It holds and administers assets for the world's largest investors, handles the record-keeping, settlement and reporting behind them, and runs State Street Global Advisors, which manages the SPDR exchange-traded funds.
customers: Asset managers, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers and central banks.
money: custody, fund administration and middle-office outsourcing
State Street Global Advisors, including SPDR ETFs
moat: Custody mandates that are extremely rarely moved, because transferring trillions in assets between custodians is slow, risky and expensive.
risks: Fee revenue falls when markets fall, since custody fees are charged on asset values
Price competition for custody mandates is persistent
Index fund fee pressure affects its asset management arm
Debt of about $25 billion funds its balance sheet
opportunities: New servicing mandates won but not yet installed give visible future revenue
Buybacks have shrunk the share count significantly
watch: New servicing wins to be installed, and fee revenue against market levels.
